findings.description: `withLockReleasedOnSignal` adds `process.once('SIGINT'|'SIGTERM', releaseLock)` around a callback that never yields. `landSession`, `runMergeGate`, `runGit`, `gh` and `auditProject` all run their children with `execFileSync`. A Node signal listener only runs when the event loop turns, and the `finally` removes the listeners before that. So `releaseLock` can never run during the run, and the lock is not released by it. Installing the listeners also replaces the default terminate behaviour, so a SIGINT or SIGTERM that arrives mid-run is caught and then dropped when the listener is removed. Before this delta, Ctrl-C killed `pup land`. Now Node keeps going and only the child in Ctrl-C's process group dies: a `git fetch` becomes a "Nothing was landed" refusal, and a killed audit stage reads as a regression. That fires the new `heldOnRegression` branch, and the land still records `landed` and exits 1. The new test passes only because it calls the listener by hand from inside the mocked `landSession`, which cannot happen at runtime.

When `git worktree remove --force` fails (for example on a locked worktree), the catch sets `removedWorktree = false`. That is the same value as "was already gone", so the CLI prints nothing about the leftover. tearDown then deletes `pup/<id>` with `update-ref -d` while the worktree that still exists has it checked out, the `landed` event is written, and every re-run refuses with "already landed". The worktree is never reported to the operator, although the comment says the operator removes it by hand. Before this delta, the throw stopped the land before the branch was deleted.

`refuseScrubbed` and `withLockReleasedOnSignal` were inserted between `refuse`'s JSDoc ("Refuse the command the caller may not run ... Every guard below reads `return refuse(…)`") and `function refuse(message: string)`. That JSDoc now sits directly above `refuseScrubbed`'s own `/** A refusal whose text came partly from the store ... */` block. `refuse` loses its documentation and the orphaned comment block attaches to nothing. Move both helpers below `refuse` so the JSDoc stays on the function it describes.

The only test for "The main checkout is on elsewhere, not main" runs with local main behind origin, so it goes through the fast-forward branch. The case this delta adds, where local main already holds origin's tip (a re-run after a partial failure, or an operator who pulled), has no test. Neither does the locked-worktree catch in tearDown (`runGit(repoPath, ['worktree', 'remove', '--force', ...])` failing).

(1) The new tests were inserted directly after the existing comment `// The gate's teardown usually removed both already; the land then has nothing to do there.` (line 425, unprefixed context). That comment now sits on 'refuses a merge commit over a head that moved past the pin' and no longer on 'lands a session whose worktree and branch are already gone' (line 614), which it describes. (2) The delta widens every `fakeGh({ state: 'MERGED', mergeCommit: ... })` call into the four-field `{ state: 'MERGED', baseRefName: 'main', headRefOid: pinned, mergeCommit: { oid: X } }`, now repeated about 24 times. Only `mergeCommit` varies in most of them. A `mergedOnGitHub(oid, overrides?)` helper next to `fakeGh` would collapse them, so the next field the land reads changes one place.

The new `if (report.heldOnRegression)` branch repeats the debt-transition loop `for (const t of report.debtTransitions) console.log(`  ${formatDebtTransition(t)}`);` from the `unmeasured` branch just above it. It then reports the kept baseline on stdout with a hand-set `process.exitCode = 1`, while its sibling kept-baseline path, `refuseKeptBaseline`, goes through `refuse()` on stderr. That gives two parallel 'Baseline kept' exits with different streams. The land-specific text ('a land does not move the bar over a regression') also now lives in the shared `pup audit` printer. A `refuseHeldBaseline` sibling next to `refuseKeptBaseline`, sharing the drift loop, would keep both kept-baseline paths on one pattern.

`auditProject` gains a fifth positional mode parameter, `onRegression: 'refresh' | 'keep' = 'refresh'`, after the optional `gateEnv`, and `AuditOutcome` gains `heldOnRegression`, defined as `hasRegression && onRegression === 'keep'`. The outcome now has two flags where one is the other ANDed with an input the caller already holds. The only caller passing `'keep'` (land.service.ts:197) could decide the hold itself. Alternatively, an options object would carry the mode instead of a trailing positional flag behind an optional argument.

The ownership guard rebuilds the launch's naming inline: `session.worktree_path !== `${req.repoPath}/.worktrees/${session.id}` || session.branch !== `pup/${session.id}``. The canonical derivation is in session-lifecycle.service.ts:189-190 (`const branch = `pup/${sessionId}`; const worktreePath = join(req.repoPath, '.worktrees', sessionId);`). The two now have to change together, and they already differ: launch uses `join`, which normalises a trailing slash or `.` segment in `repoPath`, while land uses string concatenation, which does not. A shared `sessionWorktreePath`/`sessionBranch` helper used by both would keep one source.

`assertGhAvailable(command = '`pup merge --pr`')` puts one caller's identity into the shared GitHub client as a default, and there are exactly two callers (merge-gate.service.ts:243 with no argument, land.service.ts:111). Land then passes the literal `assertGhAvailable('`pup land`')` even though `LAND_USE.command` already holds that same string in the file. Making the parameter required, and passing `LAND_USE.command` here and the merge's command at the gate, removes both the hidden default and the duplicated literal.

The new types module imports from a service: `import type { AuditOutcome } from '../audit.service.js';`. No other file in `src/core/types/` imports from a service module, and `src/core/types/audit.types.ts` already exists and holds `AuditReport`, which `AuditOutcome` extends. Moving `AuditOutcome` into `audit.types.ts` would keep the types layer free of service imports; the point of extracting `LandOutcome` was to do the same for the CLI.

In `tearDown`, `let removedWorktree = false;` is followed by `try { ...; removedWorktree = true; } catch { removedWorktree = false; }`. The assignment in the catch writes the value the variable already holds, so the catch body is dead. An empty `catch {}` with the existing WHY comment, or a `const removedWorktree = registered && tryRemove()`, says the same with less code.

`assertGhAvailable`'s JSDoc '/** Fail before the gate runs, not after ten minutes of stages. */' describes only the `pup merge --pr` caller. `pup land` now calls it too (`assertGhAvailable('`pup land`')`), and landing runs no gate stages. Neutralise it, for example 'Fail before any work starts, not partway through'. The new `command` parameter is also undocumented.

The sentence reads 'compared without case within ASCII since GitHub prints the repo in its canonical case, since it is store text and another repo's merged PR would otherwise vouch for it'. The two stacked 'since' clauses give different reasons, and the second one reads as if it belongs to the first. Split it, for example: '...is a pull request of the repo the recorded origin names (it is store text, and another repo's merged PR would otherwise vouch for it), compared without case within ASCII because GitHub prints the repo in its canonical case'.

The three containment checks call `isAncestor(req.repoPath, …)`, which runs `merge-base --is-ancestor` in the shared repo. Besides `refs/replace/*` (already noted), git there also reads `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/info/grafts` and `objects/info/commit-graph`, both writable by a session and both able to fake parent links, so a future fix for refs/replace alone (e.g. `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS`) would not close it. Impact is low: the fetched tip is real origin content a human merged; the worst case is a squash merge landing instead of refusing. Running the containment checks through `withScratchGitDir`'s runner would drop replace refs and grafts.

process_issues.description: review-context was not spawned: the delta touches no CORS/HTTP/docker/CI/settings surface. Security and maintainability ran as one instance each, not two, even though the delta is about 740 changed lines. 289 of those lines are in land.test.ts, and the trust-boundary changes are concentrated in land.service.ts and withScratchGitDir.

A compound Bash grep was blocked by the permission prompt, so the reviewer took line numbers from the Grep tool instead. The reviewer did not review the 29-line src/cli/index.test.ts delta line by line.
